Gender identity recognition rests on Gender Identity Law 21,120, in force since 27 December 2019, which lets adults change their registered name and sex on request to the Civil Registry without therapy or surgery. The 2012 Zamudio Law prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, was extended to gender expression in 2018, and treats hate-crime motivation as an aggravating criminal circumstance. Same-sex marriage and joint adoption have been legal since March 2022, and birth certificates offer a third sex option for intersex children.

The Outright International Chile country dossier, published 12 March 2026, records no Antofagasta-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding and carries no division-specific information. A visitor to the region therefore has no regionally sourced account of how these national rules are applied, or enforced, on the ground.

Nationally documented abuse is rising, and the rise is concentrated outside the two largest urban regions. Movilh's XXIV annual report (HECHOS 2025, published March 2026) records 3,620 cases and complaints of discrimination in 2025, a 27.1% increase and the highest figure in 24 years. Fourteen of Chile's 16 regions recorded increases; only ValparaÃ­so (-17.56%) and Metropolitana (-14.35%) fell.

Antofagasta accounts for 2.09% of nationally documented abuse cases, a year-on-year rise of 45.45% in 2025 and the second-largest regional increase after La AraucanÃ­a (+150%). Movilh reads the shift as hostility expanding into regions with less public debate on sexual and gender diversity. The region's 2024 share is not reproduced in this edition, so the base for the percentage change is not stated in the source.
tangentialFactors:
Chile's national politics are running a rollback effort alongside the protections now on the books. In November 2025 Congress defunded the Ministry of Social Development's Gender Identity Support Program through the 2026 Budget Law, a step the Outright International dossier places within the 2025-26 rollback and which civil society groups and the national ombudsperson for children condemned. The Ministry of Health-run programme continues to provide support in medical centres.

On 15 May 2025 the Chamber of Deputies approved the CEI 57 commission report, 56 votes to 30 with 6 abstentions. Its recommendations, non-binding, would eliminate the Gender Identity Support Program, restrict minors' progressive autonomy, ban hormonal treatment for minors and repeal the circular protecting gender identity in schools.

Regional comparisons in the Movilh table point in different directions: La AraucanÃ­a rose 150%, roughly three times Antofagasta's 45.45%, while ValparaÃ­so and Metropolitana declined. The two regions with the largest documented caseloads are the two that fell, which is consistent with Movilh's reading that documented hostility is spreading outward rather than concentrating in the capital.
localsOnly:
Residents of Antofagasta use the same gender recognition process as the rest of Chile. Adults apply to the Civil Registry; people aged 14 to 18 apply to family courts with psychosocial and family-context antecedents. On 9 April 2025 the Constitutional Court declared the 'over 14 years old' wording inapplicable as unconstitutional in a case brought by the mother of a 10-year-old trans girl, and that ruling applies only to that case.

Health care is a resident-level entitlement with contested edges. The public health system has funded sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy since 2013, and a 2011 Ministry of Health circular obliges all care centres to register transgender patients by their social name. Circular 7 of June 2024 suggested deferring the start of new gonadotropin-releasing hormone blockers and cross-sex hormone therapy in adolescents until national guidelines are published, while the Medical College noted that physicians may still prescribe. On 9 January 2025 the Constitutional Court, by seven votes to three, annulled section 46 of the 2025 Budget Law, which had barred the Ministry of Health from financing hormone therapies for trans children and adolescents. The Crece con Orgullo programme has run since 2023 for children and adolescents aged 3 to 17.

Detention carries specific rules nationally. GendarmerÃ­a de Chile's national director signed a protocol guaranteeing the gender identity of trans detainees, providing placement by assumed gender, segmented housing and entry examinations, with a standing committee of GendarmerÃ­a and undersecretariat representatives overseeing implementation, including access rules for trans visitors.

Migration rules also reference gender identity. The Migration and Immigration Law of 11 April 2021 bans arbitrary discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity and offers protection to LGBT immigrants seeking asylum. Article 10 provides that recognised asylum seekers may be granted complementary protection, and no foreigner holding complementary protection may be expelled or returned to a country where their right to life, physical integrity or personal freedom is at risk on grounds including sexual orientation or gender identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Antofagasta-specific violence incident, arrest, prosecution or court decision appears in the source inventory. The trans homicide documented nationally in 2023 and the September 2021 hotel assault in Santiago are located in other regions and are not attributable to Antofagasta.

Whether the GendarmerÃ­a detention protocol, the 2011 social-name circular and the Ministry of Health-run support programme are implemented in Antofagasta facilities is not sourced. The regional placement of Crece con Orgullo sessions is likewise unresolved in these materials.

The 2024 Antofagasta share of documented abuse cases is not reproduced in the 2025 edition of the Movilh report, so the 2025 figure of 2.09% cannot be checked against a prior-year baseline. Movilh's counts measure reports received, not convictions or verified findings.

The CEI 57 report is a non-binding recommendation of one chamber of Congress and does not change law in effect; its status as a proposal, rather than an operative restriction, is stated here on the basis of the source description alone.
